facts.text: The registration supplies the constructor kwargs, including time_step 0.2 s, distance_threshold 0.5 m and num_scan_stack 1
The registration sets the linear velocity range to [0, 0.5] and the rotational velocity range to [-0.64, 0.64]
The action space is a two-element Box: low [linvel_range[0], rotvel_range[0]] and high [linvel_range[1], rotvel_range[1]], dtype float32
The observation space is a Dict of the scan-plus-pose observation (num_scan_stack * robot.n_angles + 7), a two-element achieved_goal and a two-element desired_goal; all are unbounded float32 Boxes
KetiRobot reports 512 lidar angles, angle_min -3.141592, angle_max 3.141592, angle_increment 0.0122718463 and range_max 25 m
KetiRobot.set_vel applies the [linear, rotational] velocity for time_step with a 0.14474 m rotation-centre offset and wraps theta modulo 2*pi
A step applies the action with robot.set_vel, computes the reward, done and info, and returns (observation, reward, done, info)

step prints a message when the linear or rotational velocity is outside its registered range but applies the action unclipped (the np.clip lines are commented out); the rotational upper-bound check compares action[0]
The terminal flag is the logical OR of success (goal distance below distance_threshold) and crash (any scan range below scan_threshold)
The reward adds the factors reward_success, reward_crash, reward_progress, reward_forward, reward_rotation and reward_discomfort, each scaled by reward_scale
The registration sets reward_scale 15 and the success, crash, progress, forward, rotation and discomfort factors to 1, 1, 0.001, 0.0, 0.005 and 0.01
A reset samples the environment parameters and map, creates the robot and humans, and returns the initial observation without taking a reset argument
The upstream package declares matplotlib, pandas, rospkg, netifaces, gym 0.10.5, opencv-python, PyQt5, torch, pyastar2d, pymap2d, pyrangelibc and pyrvo2 as install requirements
The project is an OpenAI-gym compatible navigation simulator that can be integrated into ROS

determinism.notes: the checked fake starts every episode from the same fixed pose and has no random draws, so a reset reproduces its observation; the bridge records a reset seed, but the upstream reset() takes no seed argument and NavGymEnv exposes no seed() method, so the seed does not vary the upstream scene or the fake

fidelity.engine: analytic: open-space kinematic stand-in for NavGym-v0 (no crowd or map model)
gaps: the checked fake is an open-space kinematic stand-in: it has no generated indoor/outdoor map, crowd, human policy, lidar ray casting, collision, discomfort or scan noise, and its trajectories were never compared with the upstream simulator
the scan is a constant maximum-range return and the crash terminal is therefore never reached in the fake; only the goal-distance success terminal is exercised
the fake keeps the upstream step and reset shapes, the 512-angle scan length, the 200 ms timestep and the two-element velocity action, but it is not the upstream crowd simulation

the upstream constructor needs torch, OpenCV, pyastar2d, range_libc, CMap2D, pose2d and the human_policy.pth policy; none of them is installed where the gate runs, and package code never imports or runs the clone
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0 and only cap.world.step.v1 advances simulated time
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state/set_state and the bridge has no checkpoint profile for this package

the upstream registers NavGym-v0 with gym 0.10.5 (gym.envs.registration, __init__.py:1), not Gymnasium, and its reward indexes with the np.bool alias (env.py:557-565) that current NumPy releases no longer define; no live gymnasium.make('NavGym-v0'), reset or step was run, and a live backend would need the upstream's old dependency set
the upstream step applies out-of-range actions unclipped (env.py:606-613); the bridge refuses any action outside the Box, so it is stricter than the upstream

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulated world stops advancing: after an e-stop the runtime refuses step and reset until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment has no native stop method and the readable state is kept
